clue.text: Intelligence, from Iceland's story-town

parts.note: a saga is a heroic prose tale of medieval Iceland
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Wisdom is said to come out of some saga-town in Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'story-town' joins the two pieces in the surface; read them one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd wisdom, a synonym for intelligence or good judgement.

clue.text: The substitute who no: longer sits out

definitions.text: The substitute who no: longer sits out

parts.words: The substitute who no: longer sits out
parts.note: a reserve who stops sitting on the sidelines gets up and takes part, replacing someone

explanation.surface: A reserve player called off the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of sitting out is standing in, and the person doing so is a replacement.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute or understudy who takes another's place.

clue.text: For whom the, thumb could be mightier than the sword

definitions.text: For whom the, thumb could be mightier than the sword

parts.words: For whom the, thumb could be mightier than the sword
parts.note: in the Roman arena the crowd's thumb signal decided whether a beaten fighter lived or died, whatever his skill with the blade

explanation.surface: A twist on 'the pen is mightier than the sword'.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the pen beats the sword; for a Roman arena fighter the spectators' thumbs, up or down, mattered more than his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman arena fighter whose fate after defeat rested on the crowd's thumb gesture.

clue.text: Clog work in French China

indicators.note: in means the short word for work goes inside the French name

parts.note: Chine is the French name for China
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Doing a job in a porcelain factory in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain; it is the country, in French, and 'in' signals the insertion. A chopine was a Venetian platform shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopine was a high platform shoe worn in Renaissance Europe, a thick-soled overshoe like a clog.

clue.text: Castor and Pollux are-without, for example, back pains

indicators.note: being without means standing outside, so the twins enclose the next piece

parts.note: Castor and Pollux are the twins of Greek myth and of the constellation Gemini

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation before it is turned round

explanation.surface: The heavenly twins go missing, and so does something else, leaving backache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking, and 'back' turns the abbreviation. 'back pains' tempts as one phrase, but 'back' is the reversal and 'pains' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinges are sudden sharp pangs of pain.

clue.text: An artist has gone back to' the desert

indicators.note: going back means the whole string of pieces before it is read from right to left

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter has retreated into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone back' turns the whole run A + RA + HAS, giving SAHARA. RA (Royal Academician) is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sahara is the great desert of North Africa, the desert above all others.

clue.text: .Hearty: legal gentleman

parts.note: a legal gentleman is a lawyer, and one whose manner is hearty and attentive is solicitous, giving the lawyer's title

explanation.surface: A jovial lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of the English lawyer who advises clients sounds as though it means a solicitous, warm-hearted person.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is the English lawyer who advises clients directly and prepares legal documents.

clue.text: An'18th :century dandy is upset about nothing, praise the Lord.!

indicators.note: about means the dandy's name goes around the letter for nothing
upset, in a down clue, means the words before it, the article and the dandy, are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Beau Nash was the celebrated dandy who ruled fashion at Bath in the 18th century
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A Georgian fop in a state over nothing, crying out to God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AN plus the dandy's name into HSANNA, and 'about' puts O inside it. Beau Nash was master of ceremonies at Bath, an English spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a Hebrew-derived cry of worship and adoration, an exclamation glorifying God.

clue.text: The seclusion of the withdrawing-room?

parts.note: a drawing room was originally a withdrawing room, a place to withdraw to, and a place of withdrawal is a sanctuary

explanation.surface: The privacy of a Victorian parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing-room' is the old full name of the drawing room; read literally it is a room for withdrawing, and withdrawal into seclusion is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded place of withdrawal, or the act of withdrawing.

clue.text: Such knowledge should 'be' put into operation

definitions.text: Such knowledge should 'be' put into operation

parts.words: Such knowledge should 'be' put into operation
parts.note: reads like advice to apply learning, but the operation is a surgical one, where knowledge of the body's structure is needed

explanation.surface: A maxim that learning should be applied in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operation' is a surgeon's operation, not an action; the knowledge a surgeon brings to it is of bodily structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge of bodily structure, the kind a surgeon needs, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: But George Eliot 'made him Adam's brother

definitions.text: But George Eliot 'made him Adam's brother

parts.words: But George Eliot 'made him Adam's brother
parts.note: in Genesis this man is Adam's third son, but in George Eliot's novel Adam Bede he is Adam's brother

explanation.surface: A literary correction: the novelist changed a Biblical family tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's Adam is the first man, and his son born after Abel's death is this figure; George Eliot's 1859 novel Adam Bede gives the hero a brother of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves the third son of the first man in Genesis and the hero's brother in Eliot's novel.

clue.text: With St. Christopher's blessing it needs no other endorsement

definitions.text: With St. Christopher's blessing it needs no other endorsement

parts.words: With St. Christopher's blessing it needs no other endorsement
parts.note: St Christopher is the patron saint of travellers, and an endorsement is a penalty mark recorded on a motorist's permit

explanation.surface: A document blessed by the travellers' saint wants no further approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endorsement' looks like approval, but in Britain an endorsement is a penalty for a motoring offence stamped on the document; a careful driver wants none.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the permit a motorist carries, which British courts mark with endorsements for offences.

clue.text: Arranged ten-star talks about nothing much

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the hyphenated word that follows are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Idle chatter about a ten-star something, organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges the seven letters of TENSTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter is to talk at length about trivial things, a verb in the third person like 'talks'.

clue.text: Respected engineer turned up on the board

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is the crossword's usual engineer

indicators.note: turned means the little word after it is flipped, which in a down clue reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A respected engineer has risen to a seat on the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' flips UP to PU. RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputable means of good standing, held in esteem, like 'respected'.

clue.text: Pinch the end off in secrecy

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, in informal British use

indicators.note: the end off means the last letter of the little word before it is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Snipping the tip from something while nobody watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch' looks like a squeeze; it is slang for thieving. 'end off' drops E from THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is furtive, secret action, a synonym for secrecy.

clue.text: Homer's brow noted for depth. Attic brows for?

definitions.text: Homer's brow noted for depth. Attic brows for?

parts.words: Homer's brow noted for depth. Attic brows for?
parts.note: a profound brow like Homer's shows depth, while Attic, which is Greek but also a top-floor room, calls for height; a high-browed quality of elevation fills the blank

explanation.surface: Homer's forehead was famed for profundity; what were Athenian foreheads known for?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' means Athenian, Greek like Homer, but an attic is also a loft, the top of a house; so where Homer has depth, Attic brows have height.
explanation.definitionFit: Loftiness is elevation, of height or of thought and style, the counterpart of depth.

clue.text: Policemen generally take their sergeant for an 8 pinch

parts.note: the police force is policemen taken as a body
PS is the abbreviation for police sergeant

explanation.surface: Constables collectively escort their sergeant to a spot of theft.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points to the answer at 8 across, ANATOMICAL: the instrument gives a surgical pinch. 'pinch' again suggests theft, as at 13.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical tongs grip and hold tissue during an operation, so they deliver a surgeon's pinch.

clue.text: Heads the side

parts.note: on a coin the face bearing the head is the principal face, as opposed to the reverse

explanation.surface: Someone captains or leads the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads the side' reads as leading a team; it is the heads face of a coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse is the face of a coin carrying the principal design, usually the monarch's head.

clue.text: Whodunnit ?

parts.note: read as the question 'who done it?', it asks for the person responsible for a crime

explanation.walkthrough: A whodunnit is a detective story; taken literally as a question, its answer is the guilty party.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person guilty of a crime, the one who did it.

clue.text: Trade in jam ?

definitions.meaning: commerce, especially illicit dealing in goods
what is stuck in a road jam is the cars and lorries on it

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both illicit dealing and the vehicles on a road, which is what a jam holds still.

clue.text: The cheat does not buy his cards

definitions.text: The cheat does not buy his cards

parts.words: The cheat does not buy his cards
parts.note: a swindler is a crook, and in pontoon a player who takes a card face up without paying for it is said to twist

explanation.surface: A card sharp won't pay for his hand.
explanation.walkthrough: In pontoon (the British name for blackjack), you either buy a card or twist, taking one face up free; the one who twists is also a word for a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a dishonest person, and also one who twists rather than buys at pontoon.

clue.text: A rag-man makes one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters before it are made into a new word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A rag-and-bone man fashions something.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost its opening 'A'; the scan prints it. 'makes' rearranges ARAGMAN, and the result is exactly what such a rearrangement is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another's letters is what the rag-man phrase becomes when shuffled.

clue.text: Strive to swindle nurse

parts.note: to con is to swindle
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: Trying to cheat a hospital nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to struggle or compete, to strive against difficulty.

clue.text: Aunt Diana has liver trouble, though she takes good care of herself

definitions.text: she takes good care of herself

indicators.note: liver trouble in the surface is an ailment, but here trouble tells you to disturb the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: An aunt suffers from her liver yet looks after herself carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liver trouble' reads as illness; 'trouble' is the anagram signal for AUNTDIANA plus LIVER, fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A valetudinarian is a hypochondriac, someone anxiously preoccupied with their own health.

clue.text: Remus's little brother

parts.note: Uncle Remus, the storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris, uses a clipped dialect form of brother in names like the Rabbit's

explanation.surface: Looks like a reference to Romulus and Remus, Rome's founding twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus is not Romulus's twin here but Uncle Remus, whose tales feature Brer Rabbit and Brer Fox; 'little' because the dialect word is a shortened brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In the dialect of the Uncle Remus stories, this clipped title stands for brother.

clue.text: Lake that's churned up ?

parts.note: the name of a Lake District lake splits into the dairy product made by churning and an old word for a lake

explanation.surface: A stormy lake, its waters whipped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Churning cream makes butter, and a mere is a lake, so a churned lake is a butter-mere. Buttermere is a lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttermere is a lake in Cumbria's Lake District, its name read here as a lake of churned cream.

clue.text: The Captain's pretty full of fish

definitions.text: The Captain's pretty full of fish

parts.words: The Captain's pretty full of fish
parts.note: Captain ... is the hero of C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne's sea stories, and 'a pretty ... of fish' is an idiom for a muddle

explanation.surface: A ship's master who is decidedly stuffed with fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Kettle was a popular fictional sea captain; 'a pretty kettle of fish' means an awkward mess, so the vessel in the idiom is pretty and full of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional captain's surname is also the cooking pot of the idiom about a muddle.

clue.text: More dips may be undertaken

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters before it could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: More bathing sessions may be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges MOREDIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something promised has been pledged, that is, undertaken as a commitment.
